items.passage: When your family moved into the downstairs apartment in Vermont, you were sure you would not stay long enough to learn anyone's name. Casey, the landlord's son, kept a plot at the community garden behind the church, and in April he handed you a trowel without asking whether you wanted one. You worked beside him in silence, pulling stones from cold soil that seemed to resist every seed. By June, though, your row of beans had begun to climb the strings, and you caught yourself checking on them before school. Reid, Casey's younger cousin, teased you for talking to the leaves. You did not stop. What had felt like borrowed ground had become, almost without your noticing, a place you were ______ to leave.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: eager
embarrassed
required
reluctant
items.explanation: 지문 초반에서 화자는 오래 머물지 않을 것이라 확신했지만, 6월에는 학교 가기 전에 콩을 확인하고 놀림을 받아도 멈추지 않는다. 또한 '빌린 땅'이 어느새 자기 자리가 되었다고 말하므로 빈칸에는 떠나기 싫어하는 마음이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 D 'reluctant'가 가장 적절하다. A는 처음의 태도와는 맞지만 변화된 마음과 반대이며, B와 C는 외부의 금지나 의무를 뜻해 정서 변화와 무관하다.

items.passage: Lagos traffic had finally thinned, and the night bus rattled along the expressway with its windows half open. Babatunde, a park ranger heading home from a conference, had given up his seat to Ahanu, a hiker who had missed the last shuttle from the forest reserve and looked as if he had walked the whole way. For twenty minutes they argued about whether the driver should stop for a woman waving at the roadside. Ahanu insisted it was dangerous; Babatunde called him timid. Then Ahanu said, quietly, that he had lost his trail map that morning and spent four hours believing no one would find him. Babatunde stopped talking. He looked at the dark shapes of palms sliding past and, after a while, offered the hiker half of the bread in his bag. Neither mentioned the woman again.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the passage?
options: It moves from relief about the bus ride to fear about the dangers of the road at night.
It moves from mild amusement at the driver to open anger at the passengers who complain.
It moves from combative bickering to subdued sympathy once a deeper fear is revealed.
It moves from cheerful curiosity about the hiker to regret over the ranger's long conference.
items.explanation: 지문 전반부에서 두 사람은 운전사가 멈춰야 하는지를 두고 '겁쟁이'라 부르며 다툰다. 그러나 Ahanu가 길을 잃고 네 시간 동안 아무도 자신을 찾지 못할 것이라 믿었다고 털어놓자 Babatunde는 말을 멈추고 빵을 나눠 준다. 따라서 어조는 언쟁에서 조용한 공감으로 바뀌므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '두려움'이라는 소재만 빌렸고, B와 D는 지문에 없는 감정이나 대상을 내세운다.

items.passage: Smelling of rosin and damp wood, the music room in Chiang Mai was empty except for Lan, who sat at the piano refusing to play. Ottilie, the old fishmonger who delivered to the school kitchen on Thursdays, had come in to fetch his crate and found the boy there. Two weeks earlier Lan had accused him, loudly and in front of classmates, of cheating his mother on the weight of a catfish. Ottilie had said nothing then. Now he set down the crate and asked whether the piano was broken. Lan shrugged. The old man pressed a single key, then another, finding a children's song with two clumsy fingers. Lan winced, then laughed despite himself, and slid over on the bench. They played it badly together while the rain thickened on the windows, and the scale near the door went on rusting.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the passage?
options: It shifts from playful teasing between friends to bitter resentment over a past accusation.
It shifts from nostalgic memories of the school to anxiety about the approaching storm.
It shifts from formal politeness during the delivery to impatience with an untalented pupil.
It shifts from strained wariness after a quarrel to a hesitant, gentle reconciliation.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분은 Lan이 두 주 전 Ottilie를 공개적으로 비난한 일과 피아노를 치지 않으려는 냉랭한 분위기를 보여 준다. 이후 Ottilie가 서툰 손가락으로 동요를 치자 Lan이 웃으며 자리를 내주고 함께 연주한다. 따라서 긴장된 경계에서 조심스러운 화해로 바뀌는 D가 정답이다. A는 순서를 거꾸로 놓았고, B와 C는 지문에 없는 향수나 짜증을 내세운다.

items.passage:
What do I carry, Eunseo asks, when I carry your words?
On the terrace above Busan the laundry snaps like flags,
and Minjun's sentences arrive heavy, one by one,
for me to turn into another tongue.
I trimmed them all week: a name left out,
a date blurred, a brother's debt unspoken,
because the man across the table would have used it.
I called it accuracy. I called it craft.
But tonight, the harbor lights stitching the dark,
I see that what I kept from him was a shelter,
not a mistake, a roof I raised in silence
over someone neither of us will name.
Let the wind take the shirts. I will hold this.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the poem?
options: The speaker moves from calling her omissions craft to seeing them as protection.
The speaker moves from pride in her translation to shame at having deceived her client.
The speaker moves from admiration of the harbor view to irritation with the noisy laundry.
The speaker moves from confusion about her client's language to confidence in her fluency.
items.explanation: 시의 앞부분에서 화자는 이름과 날짜를 뺀 일을 '정확성', '기술'이라고 부르며 직업적 판단으로 설명한다. 그런데 'But tonight' 이후 그 생략이 실수가 아니라 누군가를 위한 '피난처'였다고 다시 바라보고 그 침묵을 지키겠다고 말한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 수치심으로 잘못 읽었고, C와 D는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 어조 변화의 핵심과 무관하다.

items.passage: Folding chairs clattered as I stacked them along the wall of the gymnasium, where our community supper was held each month on the Navajo plateau. I was sixteen and in charge of the fry bread, and my aunt Katerina was in charge of me. All evening she corrected my dough, my oil, my posture. I resented her and said so. Our friend Defne was in the hospital in Gallup, and I wanted to tell her the doctors had stopped talking about next spring. Katerina said no, sharply, and I called her cold. Later, scrubbing the last pan, I noticed her hands shaking. She told me she had once kept the truth from her own sister and never stopped wondering if it had been a kindness. I put the pan down. For the first time I asked her what she would do, and I waited.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the passage?
options: It shifts from excitement about the supper to disappointment that few guests attended.
It shifts from defiant irritation toward the aunt to a more humble, attentive openness.
It shifts from confident certainty about the friend's illness to complete despair about it.
It shifts from affectionate teasing of the aunt to formal respect for her cooking skill.
items.explanation: 처음에 화자는 이모가 반죽과 자세까지 지적하자 원망하며 이모를 '차갑다'고 부른다. 그러나 이모의 떨리는 손과 과거 고백을 접한 뒤 처음으로 이모의 생각을 묻고 기다린다. 따라서 반항적 짜증에서 겸손하게 귀 기울이는 태도로 바뀌는 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 지문에 없는 감정이며, C는 친구의 병이라는 소재를 쓰지만 변화의 대상이 다르다.

items.passage: Three rules governed the weaving cooperative in Ohio when I was twelve: no running near the looms, no snipping another person's thread, and no crying where Clara could see you. Clara had been my grandfather's friend for fifty years, and she ran the place like a ship. The day my scarf unraveled at the county fair, in front of a judge and half my school, I broke the third rule in the parking lot. My name, Isaiah, had been printed on the tag for everyone to read. Clara found me there. I braced for a lecture. Instead she pulled from her bag a lumpy green square, crooked at every edge, and told me it was the first thing she had ever woven. My grandfather had laughed at it, she said, and then bought it for a quarter. I held it up to the light and saw where she had dropped a stitch, then picked it up again.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the passage?
options: It changes from playful humor about the rules to bitterness toward the fair's judge.
It changes from pride in the cooperative's success to worry about its uncertain future.
It changes from humiliation and dread of reproach to quiet consolation.
It changes from a child's curiosity about weaving to an adult's boredom with the craft.
items.explanation: 화자는 박람회에서 스카프가 풀리며 공개적으로 망신을 당하고 주차장에서 울며 Clara의 꾸중을 각오한다. 그러나 Clara는 자신이 처음 짠 삐뚤어진 천과 할아버지의 일화를 꺼내며 화자를 위로한다. 그러므로 굴욕과 두려움에서 위안으로 바뀌는 C가 정답이다. A는 심사위원에 대한 원망을, B와 D는 지문에 없는 걱정이나 지루함을 내세운다.

items.passage: Years later, Nadeesha would still remember the brass tuning fork Hassan carried through the ferry terminal in Colombo that morning. It had belonged to their music teacher, who had died in the spring and left it, by some clerical error, to Hassan rather than to her, the student who had practiced beside him every afternoon. Hassan was the teacher's nephew and could not sing a note. Nadeesha had stopped speaking to him in protest. Now they waited for the same boat, and she watched him turn the fork over in his hands as gulls circled the loading ramp. He struck it once against the bench. A clear tone rose above the engines, and several passengers looked up. Hassan held it out to her without a word. She did not take it yet, but she leaned close enough to hear the note fade.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the passage?
options: It describes a crowded terminal in detail and then explains why the ferry departs late.
It recounts a teacher's final lesson and then shows how the students carry out his wishes.
It contrasts two students' musical talents and then reveals which one the teacher favored.
It explains the source of a grudge and then shows a moment that begins to ease it.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 선생님의 소리굽쇠가 착오로 Hassan에게 넘어가 Nadeesha가 그와 말을 끊게 된 배경을 설명한다. 이어 선착장에서 Hassan이 소리굽쇠를 울리고 그녀에게 내밀며, 그녀가 아직 받지는 않지만 가까이 다가가는 장면이 나온다. 따라서 원한의 원인을 밝힌 뒤 그것이 누그러지기 시작하는 순간을 보여 주는 D가 정답이다. A는 배경에만 집중하고, B와 C는 지문에 없는 마지막 수업이나 선생님의 편애를 내세운다.

items.passage: By the third hour of the wedding in Cairo, the hall was so crowded that Adaeze had to stand on a chair to find her husband's brother. The twins, Edith liked to say, had always been one person split down the middle, and now they were splitting their late father's house as well. Everyone knew the elder twin had won the house in the family's chess match last winter. Edith did not know, until she overheard it near the dessert table, that he had won only because his twin had deliberately lost. Adaeze watched the two men dance with their arms around each other's shoulders, and she began to see the generous move behind the defeat. She climbed down from the chair. On the table, someone had left a cake knife resting across an untouched slice.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the passage?
options: It sets a festive scene, then reveals a hidden fact that recasts a family conflict.
It describes a wedding ceremony in order, then compares it to the customs of an earlier generation.
It presents an argument between twins, then shows the guests taking sides in their dispute.
It recounts a chess match move by move, then explains why the losing player demanded a rematch.
items.explanation: 지문은 붐비는 카이로 결혼식장이라는 축제 분위기로 시작한다. 이어 Edith가 디저트 테이블 근처에서 쌍둥이 중 한 명이 일부러 체스에서 졌다는 사실을 엿듣고, Adaeze는 그 패배 뒤의 너그러움을 보게 된다. 따라서 배경 제시 후 숨은 사실이 가족 갈등의 의미를 바꾸는 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 지문에 없는 의식 순서나 재대결을, C는 하객들의 편 가르기를 지어낸다.

items.passage: Why do we wait for explanations that never come? I asked myself that every Tuesday in the language school classroom in Krakow, where I taught Polish verbs to adults who mostly wanted to talk about the weather. Cleotilde, a widow in the front row, came for conversation, not grammar. Bronislaw, the teenager who delivered pastries to the office downstairs, sometimes lingered at the door to listen. One week Cleotilde told us that her son had reappeared after eleven years, rang her bell, and asked only whether she still kept the blue teapot. She had made him tea and asked nothing. I expected anger in her voice; I heard none. Since then I have wondered whether some questions are a kind of debt we choose not to collect. Outside, Bronislaw's bicycle bell rang twice on the cobblestones.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the passage?
options: The narrator lists common grammar errors and then explains how a student overcame them.
The narrator poses a question, recounts a student's story, and then reflects on it.
The narrator describes a son's return in detail and then predicts how the family will reconcile.
The narrator compares two students' motives and then concludes that conversation beats grammar.
items.explanation: 지문은 '왜 우리는 오지 않는 설명을 기다리는가'라는 질문으로 시작한다. 이어 Cleotilde가 11년 만에 돌아온 아들에게 아무것도 묻지 않았다는 일화를 전하고, 화자는 어떤 질문은 받아내지 않기로 한 빚과 같다고 성찰한다. 따라서 질문 제기, 관련 일화, 성찰 순서를 말하는 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 지문에 없는 문법 오류나 미래 예측을, D는 두 학생 비교라는 엉뚱한 초점을 내세운다.

items.passage: "Coffee or sleep, Gunnar, you only get one," I told him the first night I worked the galley shift on the ship out of Tromso. I was a nurse on loan to the crew, and he was my only patient, a cook recovering from a burned arm who refused to stay in his bunk. Each night he sat by the stove while I changed his dressing, and each night he told me about the winter his brother had given up a place at university so Gunnar could go to sea instead. He said it lightly, as if it were a weather report. By the fourth night I understood that he had never repaid that sacrifice and believed he never could. I, Sigrid, had made one of my own once, for a sister who never knew. We did not compare them. We simply drank the coffee and watched the dark water lift the hull.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the passage?
options: It opens with a joke between friends and then describes the hazards of working on a ship.
It introduces a sailor's injury and then explains in detail how the nurse treated the burn.
It begins with a routine exchange, reveals a burdened past, and ends in a quiet bond.
It recounts a brother's sacrifice and then argues that such debts should always be repaid.
items.explanation: 지문은 커피와 잠을 두고 한 가벼운 대사, 즉 일상적 대화로 시작한다. 이어 Gunnar가 형의 희생을 갚지 못했다는 부담을 드러내고, 화자도 자신의 희생을 떠올린 뒤 둘이 말없이 커피를 마시는 조용한 유대로 끝난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 배의 위험을, B는 치료 과정을 중심으로 잘못 보았고, D는 지문에 없는 주장을 내세운다.

items.passage: I had been Gopal's apprentice in the bookbinding workshop in Dhaka for only a year when we were hired to empty a widow's house. My name is Efua, and I was restless then; I wanted to sort everything into piles and be done by noon. Gopal moved slowly, opening each ledger and letter as if it might speak. By evening only one item remained: a ragged prayer book with its spine split in three places. I offered to throw it on the cart. __Gopal instead wrapped it in cloth and set it on his own workbench, where it stayed untouched for a week.__ When he finally began repairing it, he let me hold the thread, and I learned that some work cannot be hurried without being lost. Later the widow's grandson came to collect it, and paid in mangoes.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that the elder wanted to keep the prayer book for his own collection.
It suggests that the apprentice resented being given the simplest tasks in the workshop.
It explains why the workshop was too busy to repair the book right away.
It shows the elder's patient regard for the book, preparing the apprentice's lesson.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분에서 Gopal은 모든 장부와 편지를 천천히 펼쳐 보는 인물로 그려지고, 화자는 서둘러 정리하려 한다. 밑줄 문장에서 Gopal은 버려질 기도서를 천에 싸서 일주일 동안 작업대에 둔다. 이후 화자는 어떤 일은 서두르면 잃는다는 교훈을 얻으므로, 밑줄 문장은 노인의 인내와 존중을 보여 주며 그 교훈을 준비한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 손자에게 돌려준 결말과 맞지 않고, B와 C는 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Once, Ruoxi had believed the bus depot in Oaxaca would close before her shop did. She sold phone cards and sweet bread from a counter beside platform four, and every afternoon Valentina arrived to ask the same question: had the cousin in Puebla written back? Ruoxi always said no. __That spring, a company offered to buy the counter and the lease for more money than she had earned in a decade.__ She kept the letter folded under the cash box for a month. Valentina, still waiting for her cousin's reply, began bringing her coffee and staying through the evening rush, talking about the buses she would take once the letter came. When Ruoxi finally answered the company, she wrote only that the counter was not for sale. Outside, a driver honked twice and pulled out toward the mountains.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a chance to leave that gives the shopkeeper's choice to stay weight.
It reveals that the shopkeeper was secretly struggling to pay the depot's rising fees.
It explains why the customer visited the counter every afternoon with the same question.
It suggests that the company intended to close the depot and move the buses elsewhere.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 회사가 10년 수입보다 많은 돈으로 가게를 사겠다고 제안했다는 내용으로, 떠날 수 있는 출구를 제시한다. 이후 Ruoxi는 그 편지를 한 달간 보관하고 Valentina와 저녁을 함께 보낸 뒤 결국 팔지 않겠다고 답한다. 그러므로 이 문장은 남기로 한 결정에 무게를 더하는 기회를 소개하는 역할을 하며 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 지문에 없는 사정을 추측하고, C는 손님의 방문 이유를 잘못 연결한다.

items.passage: When I first met Tyrese, he was kneeling beside the dry fountain in a courtyard in Port of Spain, clearing leaves from a basin that had not held water in years. I had just bought the house, and I was there to plan where my mother's bed would go when she moved in from the country. Cecile, I kept telling myself, would hate the city. __Tyrese told me his own father had refused to leave his hillside until the day he could no longer climb it.__ He did not say whether that had been wise. I spent the afternoon measuring doorways and thinking less about furniture than about what my mother would lose, and what she might insist on keeping. By evening I had decided to ask her rather than tell her. Tyrese turned on the hose, and the fountain coughed rust.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why the gardener has neglected the fountain for many years.
It offers a parallel story that leads the narrator to rethink her approach.
It reveals that the gardener disapproves of the new owner's purchase of the house.
It describes the gardener's father in order to introduce a conflict over the property.
items.explanation: 화자는 어머니를 시골에서 데려올 계획만 세우며 어머니가 도시를 싫어할 것이라고 단정한다. 밑줄 문장에서 Tyrese는 언덕을 떠나지 않으려 했던 아버지 이야기를 들려주고, 이후 화자는 어머니가 잃을 것을 생각하며 통보 대신 묻기로 결심한다. 따라서 밑줄 문장은 비슷한 경험을 제시해 화자의 접근 방식을 바꾸게 하므로 B가 정답이다. A, C, D는 정원사의 태도나 재산 갈등처럼 지문에 근거가 없는 내용을 내세운다.

items.passage: Glasgow rain had pooled on the lid of the rooftop water tank where Saoirse and I used to rehearse, back when we shared a stage at a cabaret on Sauchiehall Street. I climbed up there again last winter to scatter nothing in particular, just to look. Saoirse's mother had made a lamb stew for the cast every opening night, and she never wrote the recipe down. After she died, Saoirse and I tried for years to reproduce it, arguing over thyme and barley. __Once, Ronan, the old stagehand, told us we were cooking a memory, not a stew.__ We laughed at him then. Now Saoirse lives in Cork, and when she phones, we no longer talk about ingredients. We talk about the opening nights themselves. The tank hummed under my hand, full of a cold that never quite reached the street.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that the stagehand had a better memory of the recipe than the two women did.
It reveals that the narrator and Saoirse finally abandoned cooking because of a quarrel.
It offers an insight first dismissed that anticipates the women's later shift.
It explains why the narrator has returned to the rooftop after many years away.
items.explanation: 두 사람은 오랫동안 백리향과 보리를 두고 다투며 레시피를 재현하려 했다. 밑줄 문장에서 Ronan은 그들이 스튜가 아니라 기억을 요리한다고 말하고, 당시 두 사람은 웃어넘긴다. 그러나 지금은 재료가 아니라 개막 밤 자체를 이야기하므로 그 말이 나중의 초점 변화를 예고한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 지문에 없는 사실을, D는 옥상에 온 이유를 잘못 연결한다.

items.passage: "Leave the dough, Leopoldina, it knows what to do," Wolfram said, though I had stopped being his pupil thirty years ago. We were in my bakery in Chengdu an hour before opening, and he had come, as he did every Sunday now, to watch me work. I have a habit of punching the dough twice more than it needs, a habit he spent an entire school year trying to correct in his chemistry lab, of all places. He is eighty-one. His hands tremble when he lifts a cup. Still he leans over the bowl and points, and I let him, because I know these mornings are how he goes on being a teacher. I fold the dough once, the way he wants, and leave it alone. Then the first delivery van rattles up outside, its headlights sweeping across the flour bins.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Wolfram?
options: She is irritated by his interference and wishes he would stop visiting the bakery.
She is indifferent to his advice and continues baking the way she always has.
She is fondly indulgent, letting him guide her because she values his role.
She is fearful of his judgment and anxious to prove she has become skilled.
items.explanation: 화자는 30년 전에 그의 제자가 아니게 되었지만 여전히 매주 일요일 그가 지켜보도록 허락한다. 또한 떨리는 손을 언급하면서도 그가 선생님으로 살아가는 방식이라는 것을 알기에 지시대로 반죽을 한 번만 접는다. 따라서 애정 어린 관대함을 보이는 C가 정답이다. A는 간섭에 대한 짜증으로, B는 무관심으로 잘못 읽었으며 D는 지문에 없는 두려움을 내세운다.

items.passage: Two rules held in the rented farmhouse in Galway that summer: no one read the letters alone, and no one read them after dark. Orla made the rules, and her brother kept them, mostly because he could not think of better ones. Their mother had written forty-three letters during the year she worked abroad, and the siblings opened one each evening at the kitchen table. Orla read aloud. Her brother listened and said little, because he had failed his driving test that afternoon and could not bring himself to admit it. Orla noticed his silence and did not ask; she only slowed down at the parts where their mother wrote about learning, late in life, to drive. Imani, the neighbor's girl, brought eggs at seven. Orla thanked her and set the basket on the windowsill beside the unopened envelopes.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Orla?
options: The narrator mocks her rules as rigid and pointless.
The narrator criticizes her for ignoring her brother's distress.
The narrator treats her as a distant figure whose motives are unclear.
The narrator quietly admires her tactful kindness.
items.explanation: 서술자는 Orla가 동생의 침묵을 알아차리고도 묻지 않았다고 서술한다. 또한 그녀가 어머니가 늦게 운전을 배운 대목에서 일부러 천천히 읽었다고 밝혀, 실패를 숨기는 동생을 조용히 배려하는 모습을 드러낸다. 따라서 그녀의 섬세한 친절을 조용히 존중하는 D가 정답이다. A는 규칙에 대한 조롱으로, B는 무시로 잘못 보았으며 C는 그녀의 동기가 지문에 분명히 드러난다는 점을 놓친다.

items.passage:
Hollis winds the shop clocks every Thursday,
a chore he once lost to Birdie on a bet
in the Manchester chess club, forty years back.
He still says she cheated. She still says
he moved his bishop like a man asleep.
Now she sits on the stool by the regulator
and calls out which ones run slow,
and he turns each key with the care
of someone tightening a promise.
I watch them from the counter, their quarrel
worn smooth as a pocket watch's case,
and think how a debt can turn into a vow.
Outside, the tram bells keep their own time.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Hollis and Birdie?
options: The speaker regards their old rivalry with fondness for the bond it has become.
The speaker views their quarrel with weary impatience because it has never been settled.
The speaker treats their ritual with detached curiosity about how antique clocks are maintained.
The speaker sees their partnership with concern that one of them is being treated unfairly.
items.explanation: 화자는 두 사람의 다툼을 '주머니시계 케이스처럼 닳아 매끄러워진' 것으로 묘사해 오랜 경쟁이 친숙한 것이 되었음을 보여 준다. 또한 내기의 빚이 맹세로 바뀌었다고 생각하며, 열쇠를 돌리는 모습을 약속을 조이는 손길에 비유한다. 따라서 그 경쟁을 애정 어린 시선으로 감상하는 A가 정답이다. B는 짜증으로, C는 시계 관리에 대한 관심으로, D는 불공정에 대한 우려로 잘못 읽었다.

items.passage: When my mother and I stood in line at the customs checkpoint in Tehran, carrying a garment bag between us like a sleeping child, we talked only about the wedding. Which caterer, which flowers, whether Felix's family would expect a second reception. We did not talk about my father, who had always been the one to handle the officers and the forms, and who had died in March. My mother answered the officer's questions too quickly, then too slowly. I noticed she had brought his old fountain pen to sign the declaration. Nicolas, my fiancé's brother, waved from beyond the glass, and she waved back with exaggerated cheer. I found it hard to watch and harder to look away. I have since come to think that her pretending was a kind of bravery I did not yet possess. The officer stamped our papers without looking up.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her mother?
options: The narrator is embarrassed by her mother's nervousness and wishes she had traveled alone.
The narrator is tenderly respectful, seeing courage in her mother's forced cheer.
The narrator is frustrated that her mother refuses to plan the wedding in detail.
The narrator is amused by her mother's attempts to impress the officers at the checkpoint.
items.explanation: 화자는 어머니가 질문에 너무 빨리, 또 너무 느리게 답하고 남편의 만년필을 챙겨 온 모습을 세심하게 관찰한다. 또 과장된 쾌활함을 보기 힘들면서도 눈을 뗄 수 없었다고 말하고, 그 가장을 자신에게 아직 없던 용기로 해석한다. 따라서 어머니에게 애틋한 존중을 보이는 B가 정답이다. A는 당혹감과 혼자 여행하고 싶은 마음을, C와 D는 지문에 없는 좌절이나 즐거움을 내세운다.

items.passage: Years later, I can still smell the glue pot in Jiayi's kite-maker's yard in Istanbul, where my stepfather spent every Saturday of the year my mother was in the hospital. I was fourteen and thought him clumsy and too quiet. He brought me along, Eda, the stepdaughter who would not call him anything at all, and handed me paper and bamboo. We never spoke of how sick she was. Instead he showed me how a kite needs a tail to stay steady, how a frame that is too stiff will snap in a strong wind. I rolled my eyes then. Now I understand that he was teaching the only way he knew to prepare me for what neither of us would say. The kites we made that spring still hang, faded, in my hallway, their tails curling against the wall.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her stepfather?
options: She remains resentful of him for keeping the truth about her mother from her.
She is mildly amused by his clumsiness and his serious interest in kites.
She looks back with grateful insight into his indirect way of comfort.
She feels guilty that she never thanked him for the kites they built together.
items.explanation: 화자는 열네 살 때 의붓아버지를 서툴고 말이 없는 사람으로 여기며 눈을 굴렸다고 회상한다. 그러나 지금은 연의 꼬리와 너무 단단한 뼈대에 대한 가르침이 말하지 못한 일에 대비시키려는 그의 방식이었다고 이해한다. 따라서 간접적인 위로에 대한 감사 어린 이해를 보여 주는 C가 정답이다. A는 과거의 태도에 머물러 있고, B는 서툶에 대한 즐거움으로, D는 지문에 없는 죄책감으로 잘못 읽었다.

items.passage: Static hissed from every shelf of Baraka's radio repair shop in Addis Ababa when Wanjiru brought in her late uncle's set. Baraka, a retired sailor, recognized it at once and said he had promised to fix it decades ago. Wanjiru remembered no such promise, and neither, she suspected, did he. Still, he worked on it for three evenings while she waited on a stool, and he told her stories of ports her uncle had never mentioned. On the fourth evening the radio played a song, faint but clear. Baraka seemed less pleased by the music than by the fact that she had stayed to hear it. Across the street, a vendor lowered the shutters on his stall of spices.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the passage?
options: To recount how a retired sailor repaired an old radio for a customer over several evenings
To describe the busy shops and vendors of a neighborhood in Addis Ababa at dusk
To show that kindness is always rewarded when people keep their promises to one another
To suggest that a forgotten promise serves mainly as a reason for two people to connect
items.explanation: Baraka는 Wanjiru도 자신도 기억하지 못하는 약속을 내세워 라디오를 고치며, 그동안 그녀에게 삼촌의 이야기를 들려준다. 또 그는 음악보다 그녀가 끝까지 남아 들어 주었다는 사실에 더 기뻐한다. 이 두 근거로 볼 때, 잊힌 약속은 두 사람이 이어지기 위한 구실이라는 D가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
